lessons: Keep what passed review: drain/serve root binding via compose_pipeline(watchdog=...), Stages bind/clear, notify soft/stuck identities, Drain reconcile_notifications at startup and after each dispatch, root-level activation tests. Fix only the two review findings.

Stuck signal can be dropped: _call_started is set after resolve/slot, and LLMEffect's timer can fire slightly early. Start the clock at WatchdogLLM.call entry, or write the stuck signal whenever abort_current runs on a bound in-flight call. Don't gate it on exact elapsed >= budget.
Add a stuck test that uses LLMEffect's real clock/sleep pairing, or a sleep that advances slightly under the budget. A fake sleep that advances exactly the budget hides the early-fire shortfall.
Remove Registry.slot and its asyncio.Semaphore from providers.py. A new concurrency gate is forbidden reliability machinery, and providers.py is fenced for binding support only.

Cap waits: supply an empty interval list when no real provider-cap wait happens in the Stages call path. If no production wait source exists in the fence (thresh.py owns concurrency and is unfenced), file that gap to the Suggestion Box. Don't build a gate.
reason: Two concrete, fixable review snags (stuck-signal timing tolerance, a forbidden new semaphore gate) on an otherwise green, correctly bound implementation; the same capability can fix them.
